member.name: T:CudaCSharp.SparseMatrixFormat
member.summary: The format specification enum of sparse matrix

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.SparseMatrixFormat.COOR
member.summary: Coordinate Format (COO) that stores each non-zero element's x and y coordinates which are sorted in the row-first order. Value = 000...0001

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.SparseMatrixFormat.COOC
member.summary: Coordinate Format (COO) that stores each non-zero element's x and y coordinates which are sorted in the column-first order. Value = 000...0010

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.SparseMatrixFormat.Coordinated
member.summary: Since and are so similar that it can be generalized to the Coordinate Format (COO). Value = 000...0011
member.remarks:
Since the atom formats are all orthogonal in binary, this kind of definition becomes useful.
If some custom formats are defined afterwards, this trick should still be used.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.SparseMatrixFormat.CSR
member.summary: Compressed Sparse Row Format (CSR). The only way the CSR differs from the COO format is that the array containing the row indices is compressed in CSR format, that is, the row index array only stores the LeadDim + 1 the end-of-row offsets of the value array. Value = 000...0100

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.SparseMatrixFormat.CSC
member.summary: Compressed Sparse Column Format (CSC). The only way the CSC differs from the CSR format is that the column index array instead of row indices array stores the end-of-row offsets. Value = 000...01000

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.SparseMatrixFormat.Compressed
member.summary: Since and are so similar that it can be generalized to the Compressed Format. Value = 000...01100
member.remarks:
Since the atom formats are all orthogonal in binary, this kind of definition becomes useful.
If some custom formats are defined afterwards, this trick should still be used.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.SparseMatrixFormat.RowMajor
member.summary: The row majored formats. Value = 000...0101

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.SparseMatrixFormat.ColumnMajor
member.summary: The column majored formats. Value = 000...01010

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.SparseMatrixFormat.Any
member.summary: Any of the atomic formats. Value = 111...111
member.remarks:
Since the atom formats are all orthogonal in binary, this kind of definition becomes useful.
If some custom formats are defined afterwards, this trick should still be used.

member.name: T:CudaCSharp.MatrixFillMode
member.summary:
The FillMode type indicates which part (lower or upper) of the dense matrix was filled and consequently should be used by the function.
Its values correspond to Fortran characters ‘L’ or ‘l’ (lower) and ‘U’ or ‘u’ (upper) that are often used as parameters to legacy BLAS implementations.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.MatrixFillMode.Lower
member.summary: the lower part of the matrix is filled

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.MatrixFillMode.Upper
member.summary: the upper part of the matrix is filled

member.name: T:CudaCSharp.DiagType
member.summary:
The DiagType type indicates whether the main diagonal of the dense matrix is unity and consequently should not be touched or modified by the function.
Its values correspond to Fortran characters ‘N’ or ‘n’ (non-unit) and ‘U’ or ‘u’ (unit) that are often used as parameters to legacy BLAS implementations.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.DiagType.NonUnit
member.summary: the matrix diagonal has non-unit elements

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.DiagType.Unit
member.summary: the matrix diagonal has unit elements

member.name: T:CudaCSharp.SideMode
member.summary:
The SideMode type indicates whether the dense matrix is on the left or right side in the matrix equation solved by a particular function.
Its values correspond to Fortran characters ‘L’ or ‘l’ (left) and ‘R’ or ‘r’ (right) that are often used as parameters to legacy BLAS implementations.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.SideMode.Left
member.summary: the matrix is on the left side in the equation

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.SideMode.Right
member.summary: the matrix is on the right side in the equation

member.name: T:CudaCSharp.MatrixOperation
member.summary:
The Operation type indicates which operation needs to be performed with the dense matrix.
Its values correspond to Fortran characters ‘N’ or ‘n’ (non-transpose), ‘T’ or ‘t’ (transpose) and ‘C’ or ‘c’ (conjugate transpose) that are often used as parameters to legacy BLAS implementations.

member.summary: the transpose operation is selected

member.name: T:CudaCSharp.CudaError
member.summary: Error codes returned by CUDA driver API calls

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.Success
member.summary: No errors

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorInvalidValue
member.summary: This indicates that one or more of the parameters passed to the API call is not within an acceptable range of values

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorOutOfMemory
member.summary: The API call failed because it was unable to allocate enough memory to perform the requested operation

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorNotInitialized
member.summary: The API call failed because the CUDA driver and runtime could not be initialized

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorDeinitialized
member.summary: This indicates that a CUDA Runtime API call cannot be executed because it is being called during process shut down, at a point in time after CUDA driver has been unloaded

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorProfilerDisabled
member.summary: This indicates profiler is not initialized for this run. This can happen when the application is running with external profiling tools like visual profiler.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorProfilerNotInitialized
member.summary: This error return is deprecated as of CUDA 5.0. It is no longer an error to attempt to enable/disable the profiling via ::cuProfilerStart or ::cuProfilerStop without initialization.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorProfilerAlreadyStarted
member.summary: This error return is deprecated as of CUDA 5.0. It is no longer an error to call cuProfilerStart() when profiling is already enabled.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorProfilerAlreadyStopped
member.summary: This error return is deprecated as of CUDA 5.0. It is no longer an error to call cuProfilerStop() when profiling is already disabled.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorInvalidConfiguration
member.summary: This indicates that a kernel launch is requesting resources that can never be satisfied by the current device. Requesting more shared memory per block than the device supports will trigger this error, as will requesting too many threads or blocks. See 'cudaDeviceProp' for more device limitations.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorInvalidPitchValue
member.summary: This indicates that one or more of the pitch-related parameters passed to the API call is not within the acceptable range for pitch.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorInvalidSymbol
member.summary: This indicates that the symbol name/identifier passed to the API call is not a valid name or identifier.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorInvalidHostPointer
member.summary: This indicates that at least one host pointer passed to the API call is not a valid host pointer.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorInvalidDevicePointer
member.summary: This indicates that at least one device pointer passed to the API call is not a valid device pointer.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorInvalidTexture
member.summary: This indicates that the texture passed to the API call is not a valid texture.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorInvalidTextureBinding
member.summary: This indicates that the texture binding is not valid. This occurs if you call 'cudaGetTextureAlignmentOffset()' with an unbound texture.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorInvalidChannelDescriptor
member.summary: This indicates that the channel descriptor passed to the API call is not valid. This occurs if the format is not one of the formats specified by 'cudaChannelFormatKind', or if one of the dimensions is invalid.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorInvalidMemcpyDirection
member.summary: This indicates that the direction of the passed to the API call is not one of the types specified by .

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorAddressOfConstant
member.summary: This indicated that the user has taken the address of a constant variable, which was forbidden up until the CUDA 3.1 release.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorTextureFetchFailed
member.summary: This indicated that a texture fetch was not able to be performed. This was previously used for device emulation of texture operations.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorTextureNotBound
member.summary: This indicated that a texture was not bound for access. This was previously used for device emulation of texture operations.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorSynchronizationError
member.summary: This indicated that a synchronization operation had failed. This was previously used for some device emulation functions.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorInvalidFilterSetting
member.summary: This indicates that a non-float texture was being accessed with linear filtering. This is not supported by CUDA.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorInvalidNormSetting
member.summary: This indicates that an attempt was made to read a non-float texture as a normalized float. This is not supported by CUDA.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorMixedDeviceExecution
member.summary: Mixing of device and device emulation code was not allowed.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorNotYetImplemented
member.summary: This indicates that the API call is not yet implemented. Production releases of CUDA will never return this error.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorMemoryValueTooLarge
member.summary: This indicated that an emulated device pointer exceeded the 32-bit address range.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorInsufficientDriver
member.summary: This indicates that the installed NVIDIA CUDA driver is older than the CUDA runtime library. This is not a supported configuration. Users should install an updated NVIDIA display driver to allow the application to run.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorInvalidSurface
member.summary: This indicates that the surface passed to the API call is not a valid surface.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorDuplicateVariableName
member.summary: This indicates that multiple global or constant variables (across separate CUDA source files in the application) share the same string name.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorDuplicateTextureName
member.summary: This indicates that multiple textures (across separate CUDA source files in the application) share the same string name.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorDuplicateSurfaceName
member.summary: This indicates that multiple surfaces (across separate CUDA source files in the application) share the same string name.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorDevicesUnavailable
member.summary: This indicates that all CUDA devices are busy or unavailable at the current time. Devices are often busy/unavailable due to use of 'cudaComputeModeExclusive', 'cudaComputeModeProhibited' or when long running CUDA kernels have filled up the GPU and are blocking new work from starting. They can also be unavailable due to memory constraints on a device that already has active CUDA work being performed.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorIncompatibleDriverContext
member.summary: This indicates that the current context is not compatible with this the CUDA Runtime. This can only occur if you are using CUDA Runtime/Driver interoperability and have created an existing Driver context using the driver API. The Driver context may be incompatible either because the Driver context was created using an older version of the API, because the Runtime API call expects a primary driver context and the Driver context is not primary, or because the Driver context has been destroyed. Please see 'CUDART_DRIVER' "Interactions with the CUDA Driver API" for more information.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorMissingConfiguration
member.summary: The device function being invoked (usually via 'cudaLaunchKernel()') was not previously configured via the 'cudaConfigureCall()' function.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorPriorLaunchFailure
member.summary: This indicated that a previous kernel launch failed. This was previously used for device emulation of kernel launches.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorLaunchMaxDepthExceeded
member.summary: This error indicates that a device runtime grid launch did not occur because the depth of the child grid would exceed the maximum supported number of nested grid launches.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorLaunchFileScopedTex
member.summary: This error indicates that a grid launch did not occur because the kernel uses file-scoped textures which are unsupported by the device runtime. Kernels launched via the device runtime only support textures created with the Texture Object API's.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorLaunchFileScopedSurf
member.summary: This error indicates that a grid launch did not occur because the kernel uses file-scoped surfaces which are unsupported by the device runtime. Kernels launched via the device runtime only support surfaces created with the Surface Object API's.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorSyncDepthExceeded
member.summary: This error indicates that a call to made from the device runtime failed because the call was made at grid depth greater than either the default (2 levels of grids) or user specified device limit 'cudaLimitDevRuntimeSyncDepth'. To be able to synchronize on launched grids at a greater depth successfully, the maximum nested depth at which : will be called must be specified with the 'cudaLimitDevRuntimeSyncDepth' limit to the 'cudaDeviceSetLimit' API before the host-side launch of a kernel using the device runtime. Keep in mind that additional levels of sync depth require the runtime to reserve large amounts of device memory that cannot be used for user allocations.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorLaunchPendingCountExceeded
member.summary: This error indicates that a device runtime grid launch failed because the launch would exceed the limit ::cudaLimitDevRuntimePendingLaunchCount. For this launch to proceed successfully, 'cudaDeviceSetLimit' must be called to set the 'cudaLimitDevRuntimePendingLaunchCount' to be higher than the upper bound of outstanding launches that can be issued to the device runtime. Keep in mind that raising the limit of pending device runtime launches will require the runtime to reserve device memory that cannot be used for user allocations.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorInvalidDeviceFunction
member.summary: The requested device function does not exist or is not compiled for the proper device architecture.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorNoDevice
member.summary: This indicates that no CUDA-capable devices were detected by the installed CUDA driver.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorInvalidDevice
member.summary: This indicates that the device ordinal supplied by the user does not correspond to a valid CUDA device.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorStartupFailure

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorInvalidKernelImage

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorDeviceUninitialized
member.summary: This most frequently indicates that there is no context bound to the current thread. This can also be returned if the context passed to an API call is not a valid handle (such as a context that has had ::cuCtxDestroy() invoked on it). This can also be returned if a user mixes different API versions (i.e. 3010 context with 3020 API calls). See ::cuCtxGetApiVersion() for more details.

member.summary: This indicates that asynchronous operations issued previously have not completed yet. This result is not actually an error, but must be indicated differently than (which indicates completion). Calls that may return this value include ::EventQuery() and ::cudaStreamQuery().

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorIllegalAddress
member.summary: The device encountered a load or store instruction on an invalid memory address. This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorLaunchOutOfResources
member.summary: This indicates that a launch did not occur because it did not have appropriate resources. Although this error is similar to , this error usually indicates that the user has attempted to pass too many arguments to the device kernel, or the kernel launch specifies too many threads for the kernel's register count.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorLaunchTimeout
member.summary: This indicates that the device kernel took too long to execute. This can only occur if timeouts are enabled - see the device property \ref ::cudaDeviceProp::kernelExecTimeoutEnabled "kernelExecTimeoutEnabled" for more information. This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorLaunchIncompatibleTexturing
member.summary: This error indicates a kernel launch that uses an incompatible texturing mode.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorPeerAccessAlreadyEnabled
member.summary: This error indicates that a call to ::cudaDeviceEnablePeerAccess() is trying to re-enable peer addressing on from a context which has already had peer addressing enabled.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorPeerAccessNotEnabled
member.summary: This error indicates that ::cudaDeviceDisablePeerAccess() is trying to disable peer addressing which has not been enabled yet via ::cudaDeviceEnablePeerAccess().

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorSetOnActiveProcess
member.summary: This indicates that the user has called ::cudaSetValidDevices(), ::cudaSetDeviceFlags(), ::cudaD3D9SetDirect3DDevice(), ::cudaD3D10SetDirect3DDevice, ::cudaD3D11SetDirect3DDevice(), or ::cudaVDPAUSetVDPAUDevice() after initializing the CUDA runtime by calling non-device management operations (allocating memory and launching kernels are examples of non-device management operations). This error can also be returned if using runtime/driver interoperability and there is an existing ::CUcontext active on the host thread.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorContextIsDestroyed
member.summary: This error indicates that the context current to the calling thread has been destroyed using ::cuCtxDestroy, or is a primary context which has not yet been initialized.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorAssert
member.summary: An assert triggered in device code during kernel execution. The device cannot be used again. All existing allocations are invalid. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorTooManyPeers
member.summary: This error indicates that the hardware resources required to enable peer access have been exhausted for one or more of the devices passed to ::EnablePeerAccess().

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorHostMemoryAlreadyRegistered
member.summary: This error indicates that the memory range passed to ::cudaHostRegister() has already been registered.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorHostMemoryNotRegistered
member.summary: This error indicates that the pointer passed to ::cudaHostUnregister() does not correspond to any currently registered memory region.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorHardwareStackError
member.summary: Device encountered an error in the call stack during kernel execution, possibly due to stack corruption or exceeding the stack size limit. This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorIllegalInstruction
member.summary: The device encountered an illegal instruction during kernel execution This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorMisalignedAddress
member.summary: The device encountered a load or store instruction on a memory address which is not aligned. This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorInvalidAddressSpace
member.summary: While executing a kernel, the device encountered an instruction which can only operate on memory locations in certain address spaces (global, shared, or local), but was supplied a memory address not belonging to an allowed address space. This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorInvalidPc
member.summary: The device encountered an invalid program counter. This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorLaunchFailure
member.summary: An exception occurred on the device while executing a kernel. Common causes include dereferencing an invalid device pointer and accessing out of bounds shared memory. Less common cases can be system specific - more information about these cases can be found in the system specific user guide. This leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error. To continue using CUDA, the process must be terminated and relaunched.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorCooperativeLaunchTooLarge
member.summary: This error indicates that the number of blocks launched per grid for a kernel that was launched via either ::cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel or ::cudaLaunchCooperativeKernelMultiDevice exceeds the maximum number of blocks as allowed by ::cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor or ::cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessorWithFlags times the number of multiprocessors as specified by the device attribute ::cudaDevAttrMultiProcessorCount.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorNotPermitted
member.summary: This error indicates the attempted operation is not permitted.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorNotSupported
member.summary: This error indicates the attempted operation is not supported on the current system or device.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorSystemNotReady
member.summary: This error indicates that the system is not yet ready to start any CUDA work. To continue using CUDA, verify the system configuration is in a valid state and all required driver daemons are actively running. More information about this error can be found in the system specific user guide.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorSystemDriverMismatch
member.summary: This error indicates that there is a mismatch between the versions of the display driver and the CUDA driver. Refer to the compatibility documentation for supported versions.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorCompatNotSupportedOnDevice
member.summary: This error indicates that the system was upgraded to run with forward compatibility but the visible hardware detected by CUDA does not support this configuration. Refer to the compatibility documentation for the supported hardware matrix or ensure that only supported hardware is visible during initialization via the CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES environment variable.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.CudaError.ErrorStreamCaptureUnsupported

member.name: T:CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.Xt.NativeMethods
member.summary:
The cublasXt API supports only the compute-intensive BLAS3 routines (e.g matrix-matrix operations) where the PCI transfers back and forth from the GPU can be amortized.
It takes care of allocating the memory across the designated GPUs and dispatched the workload between them and finally retrieves the results back.

member.name: M:CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.Xt.NativeMethods.cublasXtDeviceSelect(System.IntPtr,System.Int32,System.Int32[])
member.summary:
This function allows the user to provide the number of GPU devices and their respective Ids that will participate to the subsequent cublasXt API Math function calls.
This function will create a CUDA BLASXt context for every GPU provided in that list.
Currently the device configuration is static and cannot be changed between Math function calls.

member.name: M:CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.Xt.NativeMethods.cublasXtSetBlockDim(System.IntPtr,System.Int32)
member.summary:
This function allows the user to set the block dimension used for the tiling of the matrices for the subsequent Math function calls.
Matrices are split in square tiles of blockDim×blockDim dimension.
This function can be called anytime and will take effect for the following Math function calls.
The block dimension should be chosen in a way to optimize the math operation and to make sure that the PCI transfers are well overlapped with the computation.

member.name: M:CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.Xt.NativeMethods.cublasXtGetBlockDim(System.IntPtr,System.Int32@)
member.summary: This function allows the user to query the block dimension used for the tiling of the matrices.

member.name: M:CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.NativeMethods.cublasGetAtomicsMode(System.IntPtr,CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.AtomicsMode@)
member.summary:
Some routines like cublas<t>symv and cublas<t>hemv have an alternate implementation that use atomics to cumulate results. This implementation is generally significantly faster but can generate results that are not strictly identical from one run to the others. Mathematically, those different results are not significant but when debugging those differences can be prejudicial.
This function queries the atomic mode of a specific cuBLAS context.

member.name: M:CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.NativeMethods.cublasSetAtomicsMode(System.IntPtr,CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.AtomicsMode)
member.summary:
Some routines like cublas<t>symv have an alternate implementation that use atomics to cumulate results. This implementation is generally significantly faster but can generate results that are not strictly identical from one run to the others. Mathematically, those different results are not significant but when debugging those differences can be prejudicial.
This function allows or disallows the usage of atomics in the CUDA BLAS library for all routines which have an alternate implementation.

member.name: T:CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.Status
member.summary: CUBLAS status type returns

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.Status.Success
member.summary: The operation completed successfully

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.Status.NotInitialized
member.summary:
The cuBlas library was not initialized. This is usually caused by the lack of a prior call, an error in the CUDA Runtime API called by the cuSolver routine, or an error in the hardware setup.
To correct: call cuBlasCreate() prior to the function call; and check that the hardware, an appropriate version of the driver, and the cuSolver library are correctly installed.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.Status.AllocFailed
member.summary:
Resource allocation failed inside the cuBlas library. This is usually caused by a cudaMalloc() failure.
To correct: prior to the function call, deallocate previously allocated memory as much as possible.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.Status.InvalidValue
member.summary:
An unsupported value or parameter was passed to the function (a negative vector size, for example).
To correct: ensure that all the parameters being passed have valid values.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.Status.ArchMismatch
member.summary:
The function requires a feature absent from the device architecture; usually caused by the lack of support for atomic operations or double precision.
To correct: compile and run the application on a device with compute capability 2.0 or above.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.Status.ExecutionFailed
member.summary:
The GPU program failed to execute. This is often caused by a launch failure of the kernel on the GPU, which can be caused by multiple reasons.
To correct: check that the hardware, an appropriate version of the driver, and the cuSolver library are correctly installed.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.Status.InternalError
member.summary:
An internal cuSolver operation failed. This error is usually caused by a cudaMemcpyAsync() failure.
To correct: check that the hardware, an appropriate version of the driver, and the cuSolver library are correctly installed. Also, check that the memory passed as a parameter to the routine is not being deallocated prior to the routine’s completion.

member.name: T:CudaCSharp.Blas.Cuda.PointerMode
member.summary:
The PointerMode type indicates whether the scalar values are passed by reference on the host or device.
It is important to point out that if several scalar values are present in the function call, all of them must conform to the same single pointer mode.
The pointer mode can be set and retrieved using and routines, respectively.

member.name: T:CudaCSharp.General.RestartStrategy
member.summary: The strategy adopted by the thick restart Lanczos and Krylov-Shcur algorithm.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.General.RestartStrategy.Naive
member.summary: The naïve strategy which only preserve the lowest Ritz eigen-pair and converged ones.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.General.RestartStrategy.IndexBased
member.summary:
Based on the index of Ritz eigen-pairs, preserve the smallest $k$ ones:
$$k=n_c+\min{\left\{n_{\mathrm{eig}},\left(p-n_c\right)\left(\frac{2}{5}+\frac{n_{\mathrm{eig}}}{10p}\right)\right\}}$$

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.General.RestartStrategy.CurrentResidualBest
member.summary:
Based on the residual of Ritz eigen-pairs, preserve the smallest $k$ ones:
$$k=\underset{i}{\mathrm{argmax}}\left( \left| s_{n,i} \right| < \max\left\{ \sqrt{\left| s_{n,n_{\mathrm{eig}}} \right|\max_{j}\left| s_{n,j} \right|},2\left| s_{n,n_{\mathrm{eig}}} \right| \right\} \right)$$

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.General.RestartStrategy.OneStepResidualImprove
member.summary:
Based on the improvement of residual of Ritz eigen-pairs of single iteration after the restart, preserve the smallest $k$ ones:
$$k=\max{\left\{n_{\mathrm{eig}},\frac{3p+2n_c}{5}\right\}}$$

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.General.RestartStrategy.WholeIterResidualImprove
member.summary:
Based on the improvement of residual of Ritz eigen-pairs of single iteration after the restart, preserve the smallest $k$ ones:
$$k=\underset{k}{\max}{\left(p-k\right)\frac{\lambda_{k+1}-\lambda_1}{\lambda_m-\lambda_1}}$$

member.name: T:CudaCSharp.Memory.Storage`1
member.summary: The abstract wrapper class of raw device / host pointer .
member.typeparam: any certain memory layout () or () struct
member.remarks:
I must warn you that although C# has GC to periodically collect unused garbage to prevent memory leak, you should not rely on it too much. Remember to use using statement or call .
The leaked memory which will be collected GC still causes not only performance loss but also potential bugs if you do not know how GC works, since the concrete class that inherits shall be a class with finalizers thus cannot be in GC generation 0, i.e. it will not be immediately disposed when out-of-scope.
See https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/garbage-collection/ for official documentations of GC.

member.name: T:CudaCSharp.Solver.Cuda.Sparse.NativeMethods.SpQRSolveFunc`1
member.summary:
This function solves the linear system $A \vec{x} = \vec{b}$ where A is an × sparse matrix of . is the right-hand-side vector of size , and is the solution vector of size . The supported matrix type is .
The linear system is solved by sparse QR factorization, $A = Q R$. If A is singular under given tolerance, then some diagonal elements of R is zero, i.e. $|R(j, j)| < \text{tolerance}$ for some j.
The output parameter singularity is the smallest index of such j. If A is non-singular, singularity is -1. The singularity is base-0, independent of base index of A.For example, if 2nd column of A is the same as first column, then A is singular and singularity = 1 which means R(1,1)≈0.
member.param: handle to the cuSolverSP library context.
number of rows and columns of matrix A.
number of non-zeros of matrix A.
array of non-zero elements of matrix A.
integer array of + 1 elements that contains the start of every row and the end of the last row plus one.
integer array of column indices of the nonzero elements of matrix A.
right hand side vector of size .
tolerance to decide if singular or not.
no ordering if it is 0. Otherwise, symrcm, symamd, csrmetisnd is used to reduce zero fill-in.
output singularity, it is -1 if A is invertible. Otherwise, it is first index j such that R(1,1)≈0

member.summary:
The cuSolver library was not initialized. This is usually caused by the lack of a prior call, an error in the CUDA Runtime API called by the cuSolver routine, or an error in the hardware setup.
To correct: call cusolverCreate() prior to the function call; and check that the hardware, an appropriate version of the driver, and the cuSolver library are correctly installed.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.Solver.Cuda.Status.AllocFailed
member.summary:
Resource allocation failed inside the cuSolver library. This is usually caused by a cudaMalloc() failure.
To correct: prior to the function call, deallocate previously allocated memory as much as possible.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.Solver.Cuda.Status.InvalidValue
member.summary:
An unsupported value or parameter was passed to the function (a negative vector size, for example).
To correct: ensure that all the parameters being passed have valid values.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.Solver.Cuda.Status.ArchMismatch
member.summary:
The function requires a feature absent from the device architecture; usually caused by the lack of support for atomic operations or double precision.
To correct: compile and run the application on a device with compute capability 2.0 or above.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.Solver.Cuda.Status.ExecutionFailed
member.summary:
The GPU program failed to execute. This is often caused by a launch failure of the kernel on the GPU, which can be caused by multiple reasons.
To correct: check that the hardware, an appropriate version of the driver, and the cuSolver library are correctly installed.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.Solver.Cuda.Status.InternalError
member.summary:
An internal cuSolver operation failed. This error is usually caused by a cudaMemcpyAsync() failure.
To correct: check that the hardware, an appropriate version of the driver, and the cuSolver library are correctly installed. Also, check that the memory passed as a parameter to the routine is not being deallocated prior to the routine’s completion.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.Solver.Cuda.Status.MatrixTypeNotSupported
member.summary:
The matrix type is not supported by this function. This is usually caused by passing an invalid matrix descriptor to the function.
To correct: check that the fields in descrA were set correctly.

member.name: T:CudaCSharp.SparseBlas.Cuda.Status
member.summary: This is a CUDA Sparse status type returned by the library functions and it can have the following values.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.SparseBlas.Cuda.Status.Success
member.summary: The operation completed successfully.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.SparseBlas.Cuda.Status.NotInitialized
member.summary: The CUDA Sparse library was not initialized. This is usually caused by the lack of a prior call, an error in the CUDA Runtime API called by the CUSPARSE routine, or an error in the hardware setup. To correct: call prior to the function call; and check that the hardware, an appropriate version of the driver, and the CUSPARSE library are correctly installed.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.SparseBlas.Cuda.Status.AllocFailed
member.summary: "Resource allocation failed inside the CUSPARSE library. This is usually caused by a failure. To correct: prior to the function call, deallocate previously allocated memory as much as possible.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.SparseBlas.Cuda.Status.InvalidValue
member.summary: "An unsupported value or parameter was passed to the function (a negative vector size, for example). To correct: ensure that all the parameters being passed have valid values.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.SparseBlas.Cuda.Status.ArchMismatch
member.summary: The function requires a feature absent from the device architecture; usually caused by the lack of support for atomic operations or double precision. To correct: compile and run the application on a device with appropriate compute capability, which is 1.1 for 32-bit atomic operations and 1.3 for double precision.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.SparseBlas.Cuda.Status.MappingError
member.summary: An access to GPU memory space failed, which is usually caused by a failure to bind a texture. To correct: prior to the function call, unbind any previously bound textures.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.SparseBlas.Cuda.Status.ExecutionFailed
member.summary: The GPU program failed to execute. This is often caused by a launch failure of the kernel on the GPU, which can be caused by multiple reasons. To correct: check that the hardware, an appropriate version of the driver, and the CUDA Sparse library are correctly installed.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.SparseBlas.Cuda.Status.InternalError
member.summary: An internal CUDA Sparse operation failed. This error is usually caused by a failure. To correct: check that the hardware, an appropriate version of the driver, and the CUDA Sparse library are correctly installed. Also, check that the memory passed as a parameter to the routine is not being deallocated prior to the routine’s completion.

member.name: F:CudaCSharp.SparseBlas.Cuda.Status.MatrixTypeNotSupported
member.summary: The matrix type is not supported by this function. This is usually caused by passing an invalid matrix descriptor to the function. To correct: check that the fields in cusparseMatDescr_t descrA were set correctly.

member.name: T:CudaCSharp.SparseBlas.Cuda.MatrixType
